## Historical audit — S0165

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 3 is visible. Line 25 is a student model-request transcript containing earlier messages and execution results; it is not independent access to the images.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| **Goal and initial build** — line 25, `model_request`, chars [0,254714) | The stated task was a single-photo indoor reconstruction with separate meshes and a matching camera. The student’s *interpretation* was a kitchen corner with window, cabinet, paper roll, towel, sink, jug and pitcher. Its code constructed multiple assets and multipart geometry; this does not establish that the photograph actually contained or matched them. |
| **Pre-execution review** — line 25, same range | A user/harness prompt requested a model-only source audit. The student reported correcting camera side and framing, cabinet proportions and window placement, and returned a complete program. It explicitly said no render had yet occurred. This was student self-review, not identifiable teacher feedback. |
| **Iteration** — line 25, same range | Step 1 returned `ok: true`. The student diagnosed tight framing, cabinet-side depth and color/light issues, then changed lens 64 to 50 mm, aim, object positions, cabinet depth and lighting. Step 2 also returned `ok: true`. The student then diagnosed pale surfaces and misplaced sink/counter silhouettes; its next program darkened materials and lighting, moved the sink and jug, raised the faucet, enlarged the pitcher and made a hollow blender cup. Step 3 returned `ok: true`. |
| **Scene-specific checks** — line 25, same range | Code includes procedural stone, cloth and paper textures, metallic finishes and translucent materials; it also attempts parenting of the towel and jug shell, and changes ring orientation and towel shape. Those operations show intended materials, connections and pose, not verified physical attachment, visibility or visual accuracy. Camera, exposure and lights were revised; the reported image discrepancies are the student’s judgments, not independent verification. |
| **Selection and outcome** — lines 26–28, chars [0,5751), [0,353), [0,58) respectively | The final read-only student session completed with zero tool calls and responded `SELECT 3`; the subsequent `select` event records step 3. All three runner results reported successful renders. This is **formal execution and selection success**, but reconstruction correctness remains unknown without the actual images or independent geometric assessment. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update or student adoption of teacher advice is visible in this chunk. The student’s own render comparisons and revisions show autonomous exploration within the harness’s requested workflow; the final session’s zero tool calls does not negate those earlier program iterations.

**Transferable lesson versus hypothesis.** The trace illustrates separating source checks, rendered feedback and selection, while prioritizing framing and broad appearance. The particular camera, color and object adjustments are task-specific hypotheses. Whether they improved agreement, whether the parts actually connect, and whether step 3 was visually best remain unresolved; image paths and successful render logs do not answer those questions.
